lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: The EPS bar is $0.03-0.05 in four estimate sources against Q3'25 actual $0.10. The company's own filings point to roughly $0.08-0.11. Underlying Q2'26 gross margin, after removing the $17.9m IEEPA refund and the $6.4m royalty-settlement release, was about 58.9% (Q1'26 58.1%), against 55.2% in Q3'25 when IEEPA tariffs were still charged. Q2'26 opex was about $69m. Management said 'we expect to be profitable each quarter' and guided platform growth every quarter. On about $170m of revenue and $72-75m of opex that gives roughly $22-28m of operating income. This sell-side has under-forecast EPS by 1.5-4x in each of the last eight quarters.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats came every quarter but were bought unevenly. Q3'25: $0.10 vs $0.04 with a revenue beat, and the stock fell 5.19% on revenue growth and holiday caution. Q2'26: $0.19 vs $0.05 including one-offs, with a revenue miss, and it rose 22.87%. Q1'26: $0.10 vs $0.057, +5.21%. Q4'25: $0.04 vs $0.03, +4.63% (baseline history; https://ca.investing.com/equities/cricut-earnings).

findings.finding: Q3 products revenue has to rise about 23% q/q to meet management's 'H2 products growth' claim: Q3'25 products were $87.7m and Q2'26 were $71.3m (-22% y/y). Supporting it: Maker 5 launched 2026-09-04 at $349+ bundles with a two-week Cricut.com/Michaels exclusive and was reportedly out of stock on 2026-09-05. Management also said the Q2 Europe distribution timing gap is not a Q3 headwind. Against it: the launch gives less than one month of the quarter, there were continued promotions on Maker 4 and Joy Xtra, and accessories and materials keep eroding. Platform at about +5% adds roughly $4m. Net, total revenue lands at roughly $165-176m, inside a disputed $164-177m consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3'25 fell 5.19% when 'Q3 revenue growth disappointed' (https://www.itiger.com/news/1128325695), even with an EPS beat. Q2'26 rose 22.87% despite a 22% products decline and a revenue miss. Q4'24 rose 4.21% on a revenue miss. So the revenue line has been both punished and ignored.

findings.finding: Paid-subscriber growth has slowed to +3% y/y (3.10m in Q2'26, +25k q/q) from +6% in Q3'25. Management pre-flagged that subscriber trends soften in Q3 on seasonality, and it is testing higher iOS pricing for new subscribers. A flat or down sequential subscriber count is likely but was already told to the market.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q3'25, subscribers were +6% but active users were flat and 90-day engaged users were -3%; the stock fell 5.19% (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/35901592/cricut-inc-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results).

findings.finding: Margin headwinds the company itself disclosed: the Q2 10-Q says Cricut is 'beginning to experience supply-chain cost pressure related to the Middle East conflict' (fuel and petrochemical inputs; vinyl and materials are petrochemical). The call added possible gross-margin pressure from ramping AI features and a marketing ramp in H2. Existing non-IEEPA tariffs remain a headwind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q4'25, management flagged gross-margin pressure from tariffs and promotions; the stock rose 4.63% on a small beat. Margin warnings have not been punished on recent prints.

findings.finding: Residual IEEPA refund flow: $1.7m of refunds booked against inventory will reach cost of revenue as that inventory sells through. A $3.5m refund receivable was open at 2026-06-30, and the CFO said 'there are still some that we're working' beyond the large majority already received. That is a small one-off tailwind to Q3 gross margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2'26 refund-boosted quarter rose 22.87%, but that print also carried a $17.9m refund. Here the amount is a tenth of that and has no path to guidance.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-22 Cricut signed a new 5-year $300m senior secured multicurrency revolver with BMO, replacing the undrawn 2022 JPMorgan facility. It sets no dollar limit on dividends or buybacks while pro forma net leverage is at or below 2.5x, and allows the leverage cap to step up to 3.5x after a permitted acquisition over $75m. What the money buys: nothing visible needs funding. The company is debt-free with $267m cash and $19m securities, so this is capacity for capital return or M&A, not a ramp and not distress. The buyback authorization has only $21.6m left, and the semi-annual $0.10 dividend has historically been declared around the Q3 print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Capital-return announcements (special dividends of $0.40 in May 2024 and $0.75 in May 2025) came with Q1 prints that rose 20.32% (May 2025). No Q3 print has carried a special dividend.

findings.finding: Lime's own Q3 guide looks conservative against its own run-rate. The $340-360m range implies +12.7% to +19.4% y/y on Q3 2025's $301.6m, midpoint about +16%. Q2 2026 printed +24% ($304.2m vs $246.1m) on a +22% average operational fleet (407,707), and Q1 2026 printed +32%. Consensus at $346m (+14.7%) sits below the guide midpoint. If Q3 simply holds Q2's +24% that is about $374m, roughly 8% over consensus. A second-print IPO beating its own first public guide is the market's expectation for the beat in kind, not necessarily in size.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-26 Arkhouse and Cobblers Cove made a non-binding offer of $39.00 cash per share: no financing condition, equity committed at signing, whole-business-securitization debt with a committed bridge, and an open door to raising the price after diligence. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Applebee's has lagged Black Box in recent quarters (Q2 traffic down while management said only IHOP beat the benchmark), so industry strength has not reliably transmitted.

FY2025 was $219.8M, which implies H2 2025 of $108.9M (Q3 $49.0M). The low end of the reiterated $220-230M guide therefore needs H2 2026 of about $115M, roughly +5.6% y/y after a -5.3% first half. H1 adjusted free cash flow was $3.7M against $48.7M, and Applebee's commodity inflation was running +8.2% on beef. A cut to the low end, or below it, is the likely guidance line.

H1 2026 adjusted free cash flow was $3.7M against $48.7M a year earlier, unrestricted cash fell from $104.2M to $97.5M by Q2-end, and $29M of buybacks were done YTD, while the company-operated base has grown to 136 units (including 48 Applebee's taken back in June). findings.finding: Ouster has beaten the midpoint of its own revenue guide in each of the last two quarters. Q1 2026 came in at $48.6m against a $45-48m guide (+4.5% vs midpoint) and Q2 2026 at $54.6m against $49.5-52.5m (+7.1% vs midpoint). The same pattern on the Q3 guide of $54.5-57.5m (midpoint $56.0m) implies roughly $58.5-60m, against a sell-side bar of about $57.5m. Management did say on the Q2 call that upside to the guide is limited unless the Rev8 production ramp, due late in Q3, can be accelerated.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat consensus by about 6-7% ($54.6m vs ~$51.5m) and the stock fell 4.78% on a soft Q3 guide. Q1 2026 beat its guide and the stock rose 2.78%. This name sells top-line beats when the guide disappoints.

findings.finding: The print turns on the Q4 guide. FY2026 consensus of $221.5m (6 analysts) less H1 actuals of $103.2m and a ~$57m Q3 implies the street holds Q4 at about $61m. In both of the last two quarters Ouster guided the next quarter with a midpoint at or below consensus: the Q3 guide midpoint of $56.0m sat against $57.7m consensus, and the stock fell 4.8%. A Q4 midpoint of about $60m would repeat that. Q4 2025 total revenue of $62.2m also included $21.2m of mostly one-time royalties, so total revenue in Q4 2026 will look roughly flat year on year even though product revenue grows about 45%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-06): Q3 guide midpoint below consensus, stock -4.78% despite a beat. Q3 2025 (2025-11-04): -6.54%. Q4 2025 (2026-03-02), where the long-term 30-50% growth framework was reiterated: +7.26%.

findings.finding: Q2 2026 GAAP gross margin of 49% (non-GAAP 53%) included a one-time $5.4m cost reduction from IEEPA import-duty refunds, about 1,000bp, which management said will not recur. The full $4.8m receivable was collected after quarter end, and the 10-Q names no further refunds. Q3 gross margin therefore steps down sequentially, toward the low-to-mid 40s non-GAAP. Industry memory-price inflation may also hit hardware margins: Cognex guided a 75bp Q3 hit from memory prices, and DRAM contract prices roughly doubled in Q1 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin has not been the reaction line in the baseline history; the moves followed revenue guidance. Q4 2025 printed a royalty-inflated 60% GAAP margin with the stock +7.26%.

findings.finding: Counterparties and peers that reported after Ouster last spoke show robotics and physical-AI hardware demand intact. Teradyne Robotics posted a record Q3 of $96m, up about 28% year on year and profitable (8-K, 2026-10-27). RoboSense's Q3 robotics lidar volume rose 309% year on year to 145,200 units (2026-10-09). Ouster's growth comes from industrial (warehouse automation) and smart infrastructure, per its Q2 release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior Ouster reaction tied to peer prints. In the sector sessions (2026-08-03 rally, 08-18 selloff) OUST moved with AEVA and SYM in the same direction.

findings.finding: Forterra announced on 2026-10-21 an expanded multi-year partnership to put Ouster REV8 native-color lidar in its AutoDrive autonomy platform, which runs on more than 50 vehicle platforms in more than 10 countries. Together they point to a defense revenue line that management may quantify on the call.

findings.finding: There is no financing overhang into the print. Ouster raised about $98m on an ATM that is now fully used and closed, plus $191.9m in a July 2026 underwritten offering. That gives pro forma liquidity of about $455m against an adjusted EBITDA loss of about $4.5m a quarter, with no debt. The raises fund Rev8 capacity at Benchmark (target over 100,000 units a year) and inventory, which rose from $23.6m to $31.4m with raw materials up from $3.9m to $11.1m. That is a ramp, and the ramp is corroborated.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior raises (July 2026 offering, May ATM) drew -7% to -17% reactions on announcement days. No print day carried a raise.

findings.finding: On 28 July 2026 the FCC added foreign-produced power inverters to the Covered List, blocking new authorizations; 45X-eligible US-made inverters are exempt. UBS (31 Aug) said the ban could affect about 50% of the US market and upgraded SolarEdge to Buy with a $42 target on share gains, since most of its inverters and optimizers are now made in the US. The Q3 call is the first full quarter in which management can quantify share or bookings from this.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The UBS upgrade drove a rally in early September (https://www.tikr.com/blog/solaredge-stock-ubs-upgrade-buy-fcc-inverter-policy); the stock has since given it back.

That gives the Q4/2027 outlook a contracted floor that a resi-led Enphase read-through does not capture.

outside_window.finding: The Netherlands' net metering (salderingsregeling) ends on 1 January 2027 (per Enphase's Q3 release). That shifts Dutch resi demand toward storage retrofits in 2027, a market where SolarEdge is strong. The effect shows in 2027 bookings, not in this print's window, beyond whatever the Q4 guide says.
